content: Bionade is a trademarked beverage produced by Bionade GmbH, an organic, fermented, and carbonated drink originating from Germany. It is manufactured in the Bavarian town of Ostheim vor der Rhön, at a former beer brewery owned by Dieter Leipold, who is the creator of this unique beverage. Leipold's primary goal in developing Bionade was to create a drink specifically for children that contained no artificial additives and adhered to the purity standards traditionally associated with beer production. This meant that the drink would be made exclusively from natural ingredients, including malt, water, sugar, and fruit essences, without the use of corn syrup or any artificial substances. Leipold also aimed to utilize the same fermentation process used in beer production, but with one critical difference: the exclusion of alcohol. It took Leipold eight years and a total investment of €1.5 million from his family to perfect the recipe. He discovered a method to ferment a nonalcoholic beverage by converting the sugar, which would typically be transformed into alcohol, into gluconic acid instead. This gluconic acid enhanced the sweetness of the drink, allowing Leipold to use significantly less sugar compared to conventional soft drinks. The final product was flavored with options such as elderberry, lychee, orange-ginger, and herbs, and was carbonated to provide a refreshing effervescence. Since its inception in 1995, Bionade has gained popularity in Germany as an alcohol-free organic soda. Its taste is somewhat similar to lemonade, but its preparation involves fermenting malt, akin to the beer-making process. After fermentation, the drink undergoes filtration, carbonation, the addition of natural flavors, and is fortified with calcium and magnesium. Bionade is typically sold in 0.33-liter bottles, with 0.5-liter bottles being less common. The main flavors available are Elderberry (Holunder), Lychee (Litschi), Herbs (Kräuter), and Ginger-Orange (Ingwer-Orange). A newer fifth variety, known as Forte, has also been introduced. In 2006, 73 million bottles of Bionade were sold. The beverage has expanded its presence beyond Germany and is now available in Austria, Switzerland, Scandinavia, the Benelux countries, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. Plans are underway to introduce Bionade to Ireland, and there is an ambition to eventually bring it to the United States.
